headlines.title: Amazon Just Lost 40 Leo Satellites. The Bigger Problem Is the Rocket It Booked 38 Launches On
headlines.summary: Forty satellites vanished in minutes, yet Wall Street barely blinked. The real damage sits in a launch schedule with few backup rockets, a 2029 regulatory clock, and a rival that happens to be one of Amazon's own launch providers.

headlines.title: Rocket failure wipes out dozens of Amazon Leo satellites
headlines.summary: Amazon's race against Starlink hits a wall after a Vulcan rocket fails to reach orbit

headlines.title: Dozens of satellites lost in space after Amazon rocket failure
headlines.summary: Amazon has lost dozens of satellites after the rocket carrying them into space failed, dealing a setback to Jeff Bezos’s efforts to challenge Elon Musk’s Starlink.

headlines.title: US Administration Plans AI National Champions Programme Including Nvidia, Amazon and Microsoft, WSJ Reports
headlines.summary: The Trump administration is preparing to designate more than two dozen technology companies as artificial intelligence “national champions” under a proposed programme intended to support their international expansion, according to a report published by The Wall Street Journal on Sunday. Companies reportedly under consideration include Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), OpenAI (NASDAQ:OAI) and Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT).

headlines.title: United Launch Alliance Vulcan Rocket Fails After Launch, Losing 40 Amazon Leo Satellites
headlines.summary: United Launch Alliance (ULA), the rocket launch company jointly owned by Boeing (NYSE:BA) and Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT), reported that its Vulcan rocket failed shortly after launching from Florida on Sunday, resulting in the loss of 40 satellites intended for Amazon’s (NASDAQ:AMZN) Leo satellite internet network.

description: Amazon.com, Inc. engages in the retail sale of consumer products, advertising, and subscriptions service through online and physical stores in North America and internationally. The company operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). It also manufactures and sells electronic devices, including Kindle, fire tablets, fire TVs, echo, ring, blink, and eero; and develops and produces media content. In addition, the company offers programs that enable sellers to sell their products in its stores; and programs that allow authors, independent publishers, musicians, filmmakers, Twitch streamers, skill and app developers, and others to publish and sell content. Further, it provides compute, storage, Artificial intelligence, database, analytics, machine learning, and other services, as well as advertising services through programs, such as sponsored ads, display, and video advertising. Additionally, the company offers Amazon Prime, a membership program. The company's products offered through its stores include merchandise and content purchased for resale and products offered by third-party sellers. It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees. The company was incorporated in 1994 and is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.
